survey: A carved jack-o'-lantern sits on a wooden plank table, turned slightly to the left of the camera. Main parts: (1) The pumpkin body is a squat, ribbed sphere. Its vertical ribs run evenly from the stem down to the base, and the bottom flattens slightly where it rests on the boards. A contact shadow spreads to the right and behind, so it clearly sits on the surface and does not float. (2) The stem is short, green and curved, with a cut flat top. It rises from a small dimple at the centre top, where the ribs meet, which is where a real stem grows. (3) The carved face has two triangular eyes and a wide zigzag mouth. Each cut-out shows a bevelled rind wall, so the shell has real thickness. The openings glow a flat yellow from the light inside, which is the normal look of a lit jack-o'-lantern, not an invented part. The left eye looks a little narrower than the right because of the slight turn and the curve of the shell. That is perspective, not a mismatch. The mouth's teeth are all joined to the rind, so no carved piece floats free.
